title: install --into, and --from in upgrade and vendor, resolve a relative path with a logical cd: under an exported CDPATH, or with -, install writes the project under a path holding a newline, at exit 0 (from 0258's review)
body:
install resolves its target with `dstroot="$(cd "${into:-.}" 2>/dev/null && pwd)"` (lib/cmd/install:235 on main). A logical cd looks a relative name up in CDPATH and reads `-` as $OLDPWD, and in both cases it prints the directory it changed to. The capture then holds that line as well as pwd's, and install writes the project under the two-line path at exit 0. upgrade and vendor resolve `--from` the same way (lib/cmd/upgrade:186, lib/cmd/vendor:125). Found by dc's critic-shell review of 0258. vc measured it on main and filed it on 2026-10-27.

The same capture turns a directory into a path at five more places in lib/, outside the readers that own that step, and contract 0162's scan, which looks only for `cd -P`, finds none of them. cc's critic-shell review of 0243 found one of these: lib/cmd/macos's `resolved` restates cargo_place, "the one statement of where a tree devbin did not make lands". vc folded it in here on 2026-10-27, because this issue's widened scan reaches every one of them.

## Measured

vc, 2026-10-27, on main at 50981f82. devbin was run from the dev checkout under `env -i` with a scratch HOME (~/Devel/scratch/devbin-vc/meas-0258offers/: run.sh, run2.sh, measured.txt, measured2.txt).
- CDPATH was exported naming a directory that holds proj, and the cwd held a proj of its own. `install --into proj` printed "Installing devbin 0.1.15 into <cdpath>/proj" with a second line repeating the path, and exited 0. The project went into neither proj: its bin/devbin is at `$'<cdpath>/proj\n<cdpath>/proj/bin/devbin'`, under a directory whose name ends in a newline.
- With OLDPWD exported, `install --into -` did the same with OLDPWD's directory, at exit 0.
- upgrade's and vendor's `--from` (read, not run) capture the same cd, so a relative `--from` under CDPATH, or `-`, names a source with a newline in it.

Read on main at 9fecb053: every `cd ... && pwd` capture in bin/ and lib/.
- The three above, logical.
- Physical (`cd <dir> && pwd -P`), each outside physical_dir and cargo_place:
  - lib/cmd/macos:435, `resolved`. It walks up to the nearest directory that exists and appends the rest, which is cargo_place's job (lib/helpers:1361), without its refusals of `.` and `..`.
  - lib/cmd/macos:448 and :449, require_stage_outside's project root and build products.
  - lib/cmd/macos:692, publish's staging directory.
  - lib/cmd/release:180, `--from`, read from the project root. A relative one is looked up in CDPATH too.
- Outside lib/'s runtime, by design: bin/devbin:37, :44 and :45, the bootstrap that runs before helpers is sourced (contract.bats:1316-1319 says so), and lib/tmpl/test.bats:20, a template a project's own tests run before devbin loads.

## Fix

One reader in lib/helpers turns a directory argument into an absolute path, from the current directory, as the user's shell read it. It is the logical twin of physical_dir: a relative path is resolved as `./<path>`, so neither CDPATH nor `-` applies, and nothing cd prints reaches the answer. It keeps the logical path, as `cd && pwd` does now, because the derived project name follows it, and physical_dir would change that name under a linked directory. install's `--into`, and upgrade's and vendor's `--from`, ask it.

The physical captures ask physical_dir: macos's root, products and staging directory, and release's `--from`. macos's `resolved` goes, and require_stage_outside asks cargo_place for the stage, refusing what cargo_place refuses.

Contract 0162's scan (contract.bats:1314) widens from `cd -P` to any `cd ... && pwd` capture in lib/, physical or logical. physical_dir and the new reader are the only places it allows. lib/tmpl/ is outside the scan, as bin/devbin is, and the scan's comment says why.

## Done when

1. Under an exported CDPATH whose entry holds the name, `install --into <name>` installs into the cwd's `<name>`, or refuses, and writes nothing elsewhere. `install --into -` reads `-` as a path under the cwd, never as $OLDPWD. upgrade's and vendor's `--from`, and release's, read a relative path from where each says it reads one. An arm for each, red on main.
2. require_stage_outside refuses a stage whose path holds `.` or `..` past the part that exists, as cargo_place does. An arm, red on main.
3. The widened scan finds no capture in lib/ outside the two readers.
4. The landing suite passes under BSD and GNU (install, upgrade, vendor, release's files, macos and contract, with the tree scans and help), and CI is green on the pushed head.

It builds after 0258, whose target_refusal it reads beside, and after 0243, which edits lib/cmd/macos.

## Resolution

A directory argument now becomes a path only through `physical_dir` or `logical_dir`, never through CDPATH or as $OLDPWD. bin/devbin's bootstrap spells a relative dirname from ./, and macos places its stage with cargo_place, as the filesystem spells it.

**What was wrong:**
- **The --into and --from captures:** install's --into and upgrade's and vendor's --from captured a bare `cd <dir> && pwd`. A logical cd reads a relative name through an exported CDPATH and a lone `-` as $OLDPWD, and prints the directory it changed to. The capture then held that line above pwd's, so install wrote the project under a path holding a newline, at exit 0.
- **release's --from:** it was read through CDPATH too.
- **macos:** its root, products and `resolved` did the step outside the readers that own it. `resolved` was a copy of cargo_place's walk that appended `.` and `..` past the existing part as written. So a stage spelled `<state>/nope/../<project>` passed as outside and was made in the project, as did one typed in another case on a volume that folds case.
- **The scan:** contract 0162's scan looked only for `cd -P`, and found none of these.
- **The bootstrap:** bin/devbin's bootstrap read its relative dirname through CDPATH, so `bin/devbin` typed under a CDPATH entry holding a bin/ found no runtime.

**What changed:**
- lib/helpers: `logical_dir <dir> <out-var>`, physical_dir's logical twin. It spells a relative path from ./, so neither CDPATH nor `-` applies and cd prints nothing. It reads pwd's answer past a sentinel, so a trailing newline is kept.
- lib/cmd/install's --into and lib/cmd/upgrade's and lib/cmd/vendor's --from are read by logical_dir. lib/cmd/release attach's --from is read by physical_dir.
- lib/cmd/macos: `resolved` goes. require_stage_outside places the stage with cargo_place and refuses what it refuses: `.` or `..` past the part that exists, an ancestor that cannot be entered, and any status it does not read. The root and the products are read by physical_dir, and all three are placed as the filesystem spells them.
- bin/devbin's bootstrap, tests/lib/test_helper.bash and .github/wsl-smoke.sh spell a relative dirname from ./ before each cd -P.
- lib/pages/install.md, upgrade.md, vendor.md and macos.md say so.
- tests/unit/contract.bats: 0162's scan widens to every `cd ... && pwd` capture in lib/, with the allowed lines read from physical_dir's and logical_dir's bodies.
- Arms tagged (0267) in install.bats, vendor.bats, releaseattach.bats, macos.bats and dispatch.bats cover each case above.

### Evidence

- **The landing:** D (stage 7) landed on main as b7ce3b55..39283d9f, one commit per issue. This issue's is 39283d9f, `0267: a directory argument becomes a path only through physical_dir or logical_dir, never through CDPATH or as $OLDPWD, the bootstrap spells its relative dirname from ./, and macos places its stage with cargo_place as the filesystem spells it`. Its stable patch-id equals that of e3c9c8bb, stage 7's tip as dc handed it over (s7b/build). e3c9c8bb is kept in ~/Devel/scratch/devbin-dc/cited-archive.git under refs/cited/.
- **No run before the merge:** stage 7's own arms and light (s7b/run7.sh) did not run. D merged on hv's GO, under which no Claude ran a test. The evidence is the runs on main after it.
- **hv's test all on rhadamanth, green at 217adf65:** the seal is tmp/test/20261029-0817.bats.out and .bats.errors. It shows 2777 ok and 0 not ok, 5 of them skips, every test in tests/unit run once. The .errors file is empty.
- **K0116B on kovacs, green at 4d1a76b0:** the full suite, with rustup's cargo proxy first on PATH as on CI's Ubuntu runner, read by vc over ssh on kovacs: k0116b.rc 0, tmp/test/20261029-0909.bats.out 2777 ok and 0 not ok, its .errors empty, the clone's HEAD 4d1a76b0.
- **CI:** run 40851772728 at 4d1a76b0 and run 40860048152 at 25175386 both concluded success: Test on Ubuntu, Shell Script Analysis and Test Summary green, with the WSL and macOS jobs skipped.
- **Fix forward:** none of the fixes between the merge and those runs (caf77878, 217adf65, 4d1a76b0, 25175386) names 0267.

- **CI:** run 40860048152 on the pushed head 25175386, which carries the landing, read green by vc.
